subject: Error Running on a Linux Cluster

messages.author: a05ad4db1ef329a2
messages.subject: Error Running on a Linux Cluster
parts:
Hello all,

I am currently attempting to run NicheMapR on one of my universities clusters (running CentOS Linux 7). The plan is to run it in a loop using foreach as I will be covering ~93,000 points.  However, I am currently getting a crash every time I attempt to run a simple test of the micro_global model on the cluster (despite it working fine on my local machine).  On my local windows machine, I am able to get it to run for a single point, as well as running it in a loop covering a subset of 100 of my points with no issue (including running the loop in paralell). However, I am getting an immediate error when running even the default micro_global on the cluster.  It seems like it might be related to this issue (https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/issues/3?_pjax=%23js-repo-pjax-container).  However, I am new to Linux, Cluster Computing, and relatively new to NicheMapR so it might be something completely different, and maybe a cluster issue rather than a NicheMapR issue, I am not sure.  

This is the full output when I try to run the micro_global (this is a modifed version of micro_global but this works fine on my windows machine):

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Error Running on a Linux Cluster
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I'm not completely organised yet on the Linux front, so there could be something awry. You're getting a segfault and it looks like you're using your own interface script to the Fortran programs. It's possible you're not sending in the right number of items and the model is pushing through on a Windows machine but the issue is being caught on Linux. That can happen. I'd suggest for starters that you see if you can get the micro_global function to run on your system. If you get the same problem, then we know it's something more fundamental about the Linux compile. If micro_global runs, then the problem might lie in your script.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: a05ad4db1ef329a2

Hi Mike,

I appreciate the quick reply.  I just ran it on a Linux machine, with a fresh global climate download and a simple default micro_global() and it also crashed.  I also e-mailed Sean Tomlinson who you mentioned in a github comment, as he said they had a sneaky fix for what seems like a similar issue (although I am not sure if I had the best e-mail for him). Any other suggestions?  Or would looking for a Windows based cluster be the most time efficient method at this point? Thanks either way!

Vinny

Sorry for the delay - can you try again with the version I just pushed to github? I now have Ubuntu set up on a virtual machine and recompiled both the ectotherm and microclimate models.

Also, FYI, I'm about to put a new release together for the microclimate model, with some updates to the snow algorithm and a few other things, which are in the version you'll be trying now. I'll post more info on this soon.

messages.author: a05ad4db1ef329a2
messages.subject: Re: Error Running on a Linux Cluster
parts:
Hi Mike,

No worries at all, I was able to get things set up to run on my computer as a backup in the meantime.  I just tried running the simple micro_global on one of the Linux workstations and that did work this time, so thank you for that!  However, my code setup still seems to have issues with the Linux machine.  This is probably a dumb question, but do I now need to go in and edit the micro_global and ectotherm function in the updated NicheMapR package or should my old versions still theoretically work? Or is there likely some other issue on my end?

I was able to get through a test run of 9,000 sites on my Windows machine and I was having it directly append annual activity time to a csv file and that was working well.  So hopefully it is not something that Windows is just not catching.

Thanks again!

Vinny
